long_biography.plain_text:
Before becoming director-general of Institut Le Rosey, Philippe Gudin studied mathematics and economics in Paris and Geneva and worked as a cultural attaché at the French embassy in Panama. His stronger pull was education: by twenty he had already led scout groups and a summer camp for 300 children.

At Le Rosey, Gudin developed a 'school for life' model that paired bilingual academics with sport, art and community service. He oversaw new boarding houses, laboratories, music rooms and sports facilities, while the Rosey-Abantara project extended schooling in Mali. The Paul & Henri Carnal Hall eventually gave the school's cultural programme a permanent concert venue on the Rolle campus.
long_biography.html:
Before becoming director-general of Institut Le Rosey, Philippe Gudin studied mathematics and economics in Paris and Geneva and worked as a cultural attaché at the French embassy in Panama. His stronger pull was education: by twenty he had already led scout groups and a summer camp for 300 children.

At Le Rosey, Gudin developed a 'school for life' model that paired bilingual academics with sport, art and community service. He oversaw new boarding houses, laboratories, music rooms and sports facilities, while the Rosey-Abantara project extended schooling in Mali. The Paul & Henri Carnal Hall eventually gave the school's cultural programme a permanent concert venue on the Rolle campus.

uncertainties.detail: Exact name, Swiss nationality and residence, the Le Rosey institutional relationship, Versoix company location and full legal name resolve the owner at High confidence. Search results also feature a Paris-based Barclays economist named Philippe Gudin, but his economics career and French professional context belong to a different person. No independent public source reviewed confirms the upstream private-vessel relationship, so vessel evidence is not used to establish published facts or classifications.

The dossier does not infer wealth from Gudin's former director-general title. Independent reporting states that Anne and Philippe Gudin have owned Le Rosey since 1984 and recent reporting identifies Philippe as a continuing co-owner. Official history documents the institution-building work during his 35-year tenure, while the current company record retains him on the board with signing authority. The school's value and Gudin's ownership percentage are not public, so no valuation or net-worth claim is made.

Service is the least-specific supported creation industry because Gudin's documented ownership and long-term operating work centre on private education. Recent co-ownership, advisory, planning and board evidence also positively establishes Service as his current principal sector, so primary industry does not rely on the origin-sector fallback. No reliable evidence reviewed establishes a larger current wealth-producing interest in another sector.

Broad Self-made rests on positive evidence that Philippe and Anne Gudin took over an existing school from the unrelated predecessor Louis Johannot, came to own it and materially expanded it through decades of operation. The Foundation says their families supported the takeover but does not describe the form or financial importance of that support. No evidence establishes inherited Le Rosey ownership, a marriage transfer, a gift or an independent start, so the classification remains medium confidence and no narrower subtype is used. The later succession to their son does not establish how Philippe acquired his own position.

Operator reflects a continuing active relationship: Gudin is publicly identified as co-owner and adviser, remains on the company board with signing authority and has participated in campus planning. He is no longer director-general, so the biography and classification distinguish the historical executive tenure from current strategic stewardship. Founder is not used because Le Rosey was established long before the Gudins took over.

The current company record supports the middle names Albert Pierre Marcel. The Foundation biography says Gudin arrived at Le Rosey in 1980 at age 26, but that does not determine whether he was born in 1953 or 1954 without an exact date; no birth year, month, day or place is proposed. The Foundation and school pages differ on whether Christophe's succession began in 2013 or was formally completed in 2015, so the biographies avoid giving a handover year.

No dedicated Forbes profile was found. Search results distinguish a Le Rosey letter writer from the Barclays economist namesake. Le Rosey's official website is proposed as a Company Website because it documents Gudin's current advisory and institutional relationship. A possible LinkedIn page was not proposed because the available profile evidence did not provide enough independent account-specific verification; no identity-secure Instagram or personal website was found.

Private education and boarding-school ownership define Gudin's durable economic identity, but no approved active education, school or educator tag in the current catalogue represents that relationship. No broad or misleading substitute is assigned, and individual research does not create a formal candidate. The minimum useful governed tag set is therefore empty.

The short biography explains ownership, the 35-year operating tenure, family succession and current governance. The long profile instead develops Gudin's diplomatic formation, early youth leadership, educational philosophy and campus and cultural legacy. Both exclude private-vessel evidence, school valuation, tuition and enrolment figures, rankings and promotional claims.

review.notes: Terminal resolved-person dossier. Philippe Gudin is the Swiss Le Rosey co-owner and former director-general, not the Paris-based Barclays economist namesake. Independent ownership reporting, official institutional history and current company governance provide direct personal wealth-mechanism evidence. Service describes both the private-education asset that produced the documented wealth relationship and his current sector; broad Self-made is medium confidence because the takeover and decades of value-building are documented but the nature of family support and acquisition financing is not; and Operator reflects continuing co-ownership, advice, board service and strategic work after the director-general handover. The dossier fills middle names, known-for title and biography, proposes the official Company Website, and assigns no tag because the active catalogue has no education literal. Birth details, LinkedIn, Instagram, personal website and any narrower origin subtype remain unsupported. Nothing has been compiled or applied to the live owner record.
